summary.headline: MM Forgings H1 FY27 sales reached INR 978 crore on ~44,000 tons; Q2 revenue INR 551 crore with guidance for over INR 2,000 crore in FY27.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 551 crore on 24,200 tons, against 19,700 tons in Q1, with H1 turnover of INR 978 crore. Management said Q2 EBITDA was about INR 110 crore (around 20%, or 19.7% overall after a mild correction for prior-quarter price increases), and realisation rose to INR 2.15 lakh per ton from INR 2.08 lakh. PAT includes a land sale of INR 64.29 crore (profit about INR 54 crore), and DVS Industries has been merged into the company. Management guided to about 50,000 tons in H2, 90,000-95,000 tons for FY27 and above INR 2,000 crore turnover, with FY28 above 100,000 tons and INR 2,400-2,500 crore.

financial_highlights.change: management said margin should be mildly corrected for 0.5-0.7% of prior-quarter price increases

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Automotive is 85% of sales: CV 70% and PV 14%. Off-highway and tractor is 14%, down from 15% as auto grew faster.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Domestic is 66% of sales and exports 34%. India fell to 67% from 72% of sales, Europe rose to 13% from 12%, and US rose to 16.5% from 12.5%.

segments.name: Machining mix
segments.commentary: Machining rose to 65% of sales from 56%, supporting realisation gains. Machining utilisation is about 75-80%, with 25-30% headroom and new lines being added.

segments.name: Heavy forgings (16,500 ton press)
segments.commentary: The press costs INR 240 crore and is delayed 6-8 months. It is due for commissioning in Q4 FY27 with SOP by Q1 FY28, and is largely unsold so far.

segments.name: Abhinava Rizel (AR)
segments.commentary: AR started selling 300-400 motors a month from July. Target is 2,000-4,000 motors a month, with an INR 10-20 crore capex need.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 sales of about 50,000 tons, taking FY27 to 90,000-95,000 tons and turnover above INR 2,000 crore.
FY28 expected to cross 100,000 tons and INR 2,400-2,500 crore turnover, with order visibility for that range subject to global CV cycle.
Export revenue targeted to reach INR 1,000 crore over the next few years, and INR 1,200-1,500 crore by end of decade; annualised exports about INR 600 crore.
Margins expected to be positive; internal cost-reduction scope of INR 30-100 crore cited, explicitly not a committed number.
H2 capex of INR 75-80 crore (H1 INR 65 crore), total about INR 150 crore; debt expected to stay flat.
capex_capacity: Capacity is 130,000 tons after adding a 4,000-ton press at Viralimalai; annualised about 127,500 tons. Current capacity can support about 120,000 tons.
16,500-ton heavy press to be commissioned in Q4 FY27, SOP by Q1 FY28. Initial use of INR 50-100 crore annualised, rising to INR 250-400 crore with extra machining setup.
Over the last six years the company invested over INR 1,200 crore, of which INR 750+ crore went to forging.
Machining capacity headroom of about 25-30% at 70-80% utilisation, with new lines being added; management could not yet give a firm capacity figure.
Investments in crankshaft and beam lines and knuckles to raise capacity.
demand_pricing: Class 8 truck demand in the US is strong, helped by pre-buy ahead of emission norms and replacement demand; pre-buy expected to fade by Q1 FY28, after which base-load demand should remain.
Europe CV demand is described as steady and replacement-driven; the company is deepening engagement with European OEMs.
Heavy-forging competition is increasing, with Happy Forgings, Bharat Forge and Ramkrishna Forgings adding heavy presses; management sees enough demand for the top four players.
Multi-axle vehicles are back in demand, with front-axle volumes up at most OEMs.
Realisation gains came from higher machining mix plus steel and conversion price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Could guidance be framed as outperformance over industry growth rather than absolute numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will work out a comparison against industry growth to show wallet-share gains, with no commitment yet.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue can the current base support before new capex, and what are utilisation levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 130,000 tons against FY27 volume of 90,000-95,000 tons; the base can reach about 120,000 tons. Machining utilisation is about 75-80%, and the machining base can support INR 2,400-2,500 crore once new lines are added.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 16,500-ton press delayed, and is there a cost escalation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no cost escalation beyond interest. The 6-8 month delay came from vendor execution on welded foundation plates, and some customer validation delays also contributed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and cost of debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is expected to stay at about INR 1,020-1,070 crore net, or about INR 1,200 crore gross. Average cost of debt is 5.42%, down from 8.5% last year.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the realisation increase of about 9-10% sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation rose to INR 2.15 lakh per ton from INR 2.08 lakh, driven by machining mix rising to 65% from 56% and steel and conversion price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Does the heavy press open a new non-auto segment, such as the HHP genset order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the heavy press opens a new non-auto class, with some parts beyond auto weight range, while non-auto volumes are not comparable to auto. The genset order is one factor among several.

risks_watch: Management said FY28 growth depends on the global CV cycle, and North American truck demand is cyclical after pre-buy fades.
The 16,500-ton press (INR 240 crore) remains largely unsold, and OEM qualification may take 6 months to 2 years.
Return on capital pressure: about INR 800 crore spent in three years versus INR 380 crore capitalised, with ROCE averaging about 10%.
Manufacturing systems are not yet homogenised across plants after the DVS merger; management called this a long way to go.
Earnings remain heavily CV-dependent, and predictability improvements are expected only over two to three years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and export growth and on the 16,500-ton press timeline. Cautious on margins, declining to commit to the INR 30-100 crore cost-reduction range, and candid on execution delays, manufacturing-system gaps and the unsold press. Some answers were evasive, notably on machining capacity, which management said it could not yet quantify.
key_quotes: We are expecting about 50,000 tons of sales for H2, taking the overall to the region of 90,000- 95,000 tons for the year.
On manufacturing systems, we have a long way to go.
Good news is that it's now behind us, but the learning stays that we need to be far more nimbler in execution, and we are focused a lot on it.

adds.what: 4,000-ton press at Viralimalai (capacity now 130,000 tons; annualised ~127,500 tons)
16,500-ton heavy forging press, INR 240 crore, delayed 6-8 months

growth.why: FY27 turnover guided above INR 2,000 crore on 90,000-95,000 t, with H2 volume of ~50,000 t, and FY28 at INR 2,400-2,500 crore; backing is partial (Viralimalai press, machining headroom at ~75-80% utilisation, US and Europe demand) but the 16,500-t heavy press is delayed and largely unsold, and no firm order book was quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Realisation rose to INR 2.15-2.23 lakh per ton from INR 2.08 lakh on machining mix of 65% (from 56%), but management declined to commit to the INR 30-100 crore cost-reduction range and Q2 EBITDA was about 19.7% after correction.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 16,500-ton heavy press (INR 240 crore) is under construction, due Q4 FY27 with SOP by Q1 FY28 after a 6-8 month delay, while the 4,000-ton Viralimalai press is already commissioned taking capacity to 130,000 tons.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume rose to 24,200 tons from 19,700 in Q1, H2 is guided at about 50,000 tons for 90,000-95,000 in FY27, and FY28 is guided above 100,000 tons.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Machining utilisation is about 75-80% with 25-30% headroom, FY28 guidance is above 100,000 tons, and H2 FY27 capex of INR 75-80 crore is already planned, so further machining line or press announcements are probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 turnover was already raised to above INR 2,000 crore on 90,000-95,000 tons, with H1 at INR 978 crore and H2 volume of about 50,000 tons, so upside depends on US and Europe demand holding.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY28 INR 2,400-2,500 crore depends on the global CV cycle and US pre-buy fades by Q1 FY28, and the INR 240 crore press is largely unsold with OEM qualification taking 6 months to 2 years.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The 16,500-ton press opens a new non-auto heavy class, with initial use of INR 50-100 crore annualised rising to INR 250-400 crore, and AR has started selling 300-400 motors a month from July against a 2,000-4,000 target.

rows.label: Export revenue to INR 1,000 crore
rows.why: Exports are 34% of sales with US share up to 16.5% from 12.5% and Europe to 13% from 12%, and annualised exports are about INR 600 crore against a target of INR 1,000 crore over the next few years.

rows.label: Debt flat at about INR 1,200 crore gross
rows.why: Gross debt is about INR 1,200 crore and net debt INR 1,020-1,070 crore, with average cost of debt down to 5.42% from 8.5%, and H2 capex of INR 75-80 crore is expected to be funded without a rise in debt.

rows.label: Internal cost reduction INR 30-100 crore
rows.why: Management cited an INR 30-100 crore internal cost-reduction scope but explicitly declined to commit to it, so the call leans against a firm saving.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume, export growth and the 16,500-ton press timeline, but cautious on margins, declined to commit to the INR 30-100 crore cost-reduction range, and was candid on the press delay, unsold capacity and machining capacity figures. quality.why: Q2 volume rose to 24,200 tons from 19,700 tons in Q1 (about 23% QoQ) and realisation rose to INR 2.15 lakh/t from INR 2.08 lakh, helped by machining mix (65% from 56%) and price increases; however, the roughly INR 54 crore land-sale profit is a one-off in Q2 PAT, and the brief does not give a YoY revenue growth figure or say whether DVS merger consolidation contributed to growth.
